definition: Astrostatistics is a discipline which spans astrophysics, statistical analysis and data mining.
details: It is used to process the vast amount of data produced by automated scanning of the cosmos, to characterize complex datasets, and to link astronomical data to astrophysical theory. Many branches of statistics are involved in astronomical analysis including nonparametrics, multivariate regression and multivariate classification, time series analysis, and especially Bayesian inference. The field is closely related to astroinformatics.

explainer.lead: Astrostatistics uses statistics and data mining to make sense of the enormous datasets produced by observing the cosmos. It helps astronomers describe complex measurements and connect them with theories about how the universe works.

tiers.eli5: Automated telescopes can collect more information than people could reasonably inspect one piece at a time. Astrostatistics is like using careful number-crunching to find patterns in a huge box of sky observations. Those patterns can help scientists understand what they are seeing and compare it with their ideas about space.
tiers.practitioner: Practitioners apply methods such as nonparametrics, multivariate regression and classification, time-series analysis, and Bayesian inference to astronomical datasets. The work can involve characterizing observations, mining them for patterns, and comparing them with astrophysical theory; the sheer volume and complexity of the data are central challenges.
tiers.paperLevel: Astrostatistics is an interdisciplinary discipline spanning astrophysics, statistical analysis, and data mining. In a typical Bayesian formulation, observations D are used to update beliefs about theoretical parameters theta through p(theta | D) proportional to p(D | theta) p(theta). It is not a single algorithm, and its practical difficulty includes processing vast, complex datasets while choosing appropriate statistical models.

explainer.example: Suppose an automated scan records an object's brightness repeatedly, producing far too many measurements to inspect individually. Time-series analysis can characterize how the brightness changes, while Bayesian inference can combine those measurements with prior assumptions to estimate parameters of an astrophysical model and assess how well the data support it.

usedIn.detail: Links astronomical measurements to astrophysical theory through statistical analysis.

usedIn.name: Astroinformatics
usedIn.detail: Closely overlaps with astrostatistics in the computational handling and analysis of astronomical information.

explainer.intuition: Astronomical observations become scientifically useful when statistical methods separate meaningful patterns from complexity and uncertainty. Astrostatistics supplies that bridge from raw measurements to descriptions of astronomical objects and tests of astrophysical ideas.
howItWorks: Collect large volumes of measurements from automated scans of the cosmos.
Organize and characterize the resulting complex datasets.
Apply statistical or data-mining methods, such as regression, classification, time-series analysis, or Bayesian inference.
Interpret the results in relation to astrophysical theory.
explainer.whyItMatters: Without these methods, much of the information gathered by automated cosmic scanning would be difficult to process or interpret. Astrostatistics turns large observational datasets into evidence that can be compared with astrophysical theory.
misconceptions: It is not a single statistical technique; it draws on many branches of statistics and data mining.
It is not limited to finding patterns, because it also connects astronomical data with astrophysical theory.
It is closely related to astroinformatics, but the two terms are not presented as identical.
